newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-CALIFANO'S OUTBURST ADDS TO FRENCH WORRIES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CALIFANO'S OUTBURST ADDS TO FRENCH WORRIES.

text.p: By punching an opponent in a league match at the weekend, Toulouse prop Christian Califano added to the worries of an injury-prone French rugby union side aiming for a possible first grand slam in 10 years.

The French selectors, who have said that any player sent off in a league match would automatically miss the next international game, will have to do without arguably the most dynamic prop in the world against Scotland in a decisive Five Nations clash on Saturday at Parc des Princes.
Califano received his marching orders for knocking out counterpart Louis Esposito in a tense match at Grenoble on Sunday which the French champions eventually won 19-17.

"We can't pretend that he didn't do anything wrong," said French trainer Jean-Claude Skrela on Monday, just before the French squad left for their training camp in a forest outside Paris to prepare for the Scotland match. "It's a pity but we just can't pick him."
Califano will be replaced in the group of 21 players by Brive's Didier Casadei but Skrela was afraid he might also lose flyhalf Alain Penaud and scrumhalf Philippe Carbonneau, both injured.
Penaud, who has groin trouble, and Carbonneau, who twisted his ankle, were due to undergo medical checks on Monday and it was unclear whether they would be fit to play on Saturday, Skrela said.
Skrela has been unlucky since the tournament started as 17 players have been sidelined for one match or more by injury or suspension.
"We're getting used to it but still it's a nuisance," he said. "I shouldn't do it but I'm always trying to guess who will be the next one on the list. It just never stops."
Skrela blamed the increasing number of league and European Cup matches, saying the players were no longer able to recuperate before international fixtures.
If Carbonneau could not play, he would be replaced in the group by Toulouse scrumhalf Jerome Cazalbou while Castres player Eric Artiguste would be called up if Penaud was not fit, Skrela said.

One good thing about all the bad luck was that it had brought the players closer, said Skrela, who is hoping for France's first victory in the tournament since 1993 and their first grand slam since 1987.
"The spirit in the team is just like it should be," he said. "The guys stay humble and when somebody gets injured it makes them want to win even more."

Skrela, who was delighted to see his team beat England 23-20 at Twickenham on March 20, won a grand slam with France in 1977, playing alongside Jean-Pierre Rives in a formidable back row. He said his players knew what was at stake.
"To win a grand slam is really special," he said. "No player in this team has ever done it and they will give their all. They're expecting a tough match but they're ready for it."
